claim.pdf_says: PDF page 390 (printed 360) opens with the final row of the two-column Term / Subclause list that began on printed page 359: "varying-clause          13.18.64, VARYING clause"
claim.why_it_matters: The transcription renders the rest of this list as a markdown table in the page-389 slice ('| Term | Subclause |' ... '| value-clause | 13.18.63, VALUE clause (report-section format) |'), but the one row that fell past the page break is emitted as a bare paragraph in the page-390 slice, detached from the table it belongs to. The term-to-subclause mapping is still legible, so no normative content is lost, but the row is structurally orphaned and will not render or be extracted as part of the 13.15.2 meta-language term list.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified both sources independently at 300 dpi. The factual observations in the claim are accurate but they do not constitute a content discrepancy.

1) PDF page 390 (printed 360), rendered and read directly: the first body line, above the '13.15.3 Syntax rules' heading, reads 'varying-clause' at the left margin followed by tab-column whitespace and '13.18.64, VARYING clause'. Nothing else of that list appears on this page - there is no repeated column header, no rule, no continuation marker. The ISO page break itself orphans the row; the row stands alone at the top of a fresh page in the canonical source.

2) specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 16732, inside the page-390 slice, reads 'varying-clause 13.18.64, VARYING clause'. Every token of the PDF row is present and in the same order. The only textual difference is that the tab-column run of spaces is collapsed to one space, which is the whitespace normalization the transcription applies document-wide.

3) The claim's premise about the page-389 slice is also accurate (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 16711-16723 do render eleven rows as a markdown table ending at '| value-clause | 13.18.63, VALUE clause (report-section format) |'), so the row is indeed a paragraph where its siblings are table rows.

But that is exactly the exclusion the verification criteria name: the allegedly missing text is present, complete and correctly spelled; the difference is page-break furniture plus markdown block-type choice; and the meaning is unchanged. The term-to-subclause mapping 'varying-clause -> 13.18.64, VARYING clause' is fully recoverable from the transcription, and the claim concedes this ('no normative content is lost'). Moreover the markdown here mirrors the PDF's own layout rather than departing from it: the canonical source presents this row detached from its table too. A per-page transcription of a table that ISO split across a page boundary will necessarily split the table; that is a property of the slicing model, not a transcription error against the PDF.

The residual concern - that a tool extracting the 13.15.2 term list from the markdown table would miss varying-clause - is a downstream tooling ergonomics matter about how the transcription is consumed, not a divergence between the PDF and its transcription. It is worth noting that COBOL.NET's use of this list is nil either way: 13.18.64 VARYING clause is reachable directly by section number.

Incidental, out of scope for this claim and not adjudicated here: the page-390 slice ends item 14c with '...\'PICTURE N(length)\' where length is the length of the literal as specified in 8.3.3, Literals.', while the rendered PDF page 390 ends 14c at "'PICTURE N(length)'" with the trailing 'where length is...' clause carrying to the next page. That is a separate backward-merge across the same page boundary and should be filed on its own if it has not been already.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy. The row 'varying-clause 13.18.64, VARYING clause' is present in the page-390 markdown slice, complete and verbatim apart from collapsed tab whitespace, and the printed PDF page likewise carries it as an isolated line at the top of the page with no table header. The finding reduces to a markdown block-type choice (paragraph rather than a one-row continuation table) for a row ISO itself orphaned across a page break - formatting only, meaning preserved, nothing lost.
